english: Thus, at buddhahood there is the resolve for awakening. The Adornment of Clear Realization teaches three [forms]: the Dharma festival, like a musical instrument; the single-traversal path, like a river; and the Dharma embodiment, like a cloud. The same Adornment explains the generation of the ordinary mind [of awakening] that has abandoned obscurations, and so forth. The Guhyasamāja and nondual [tantras] say:[^N-C-082]

notes.problem: The three analogies and tantra grouping are abbreviated; the reference conflates Guhyasamāja and nondual into a title.
notes.treatment: Retain the three analogies as prose enumeration; bracket [forms], [of awakening], and [tantras] as contextual supplies.
notes.uncertainty: Whether nondual qualifies Guhyasamāja or names another class remains open.
notes.review_action: Check the analogies and citation grouping.

english:
Because the ordinary mind of awakening is inexhaustible,
Enlightened activity is uninterrupted.
So it is said.

Addendum. Some hold that when a buddha passes into nirvāṇa it is like a fire whose fuel is exhausted. Others say that, once disciples to be guided through embodiment are exhausted, disciples are taught through speech; the Buddha goes to Akaniṣṭha and abides there, appearing occasionally to those who have accumulated merit.

Here, that buddha as form embodiment, whose intrinsic nature is the two kinds of ordinary mind of awakening, is the wheel of the inexhaustible adornments of embodiment, speech, and awakened heart, free from all extremes. The Questions of Jönpa says:

Blessed One, skilled in dependence on causes,
Never possessing views of the two extremes,
You teach precisely the ripened results of karma.
Homage to you, free from the darkness of views.
And the Adornment of Sūtras says:

Without an apprehending subject, without faults,
Without turbidity, without abiding,
Unmoving, without elaboration regarding all phenomena—
To you I pay homage.
It is as this says.

Vajra statement. Some say that the empty Dharma embodiment has no connection to any qualities or enlightened activities of the form embodiment. Although there is no awakened heart thinking, “I shall guide these disciples in this way,” the wheel of inexhaustible adornments occurs merely as transformations in others’ appearance. Others hold that its operation is uninterrupted and occurs solely as good.

Here, the awakened heart operates even as far as views of permanence and annihilation: however many inconceivable distinctions there are in disciples’ differentiating conceptualization and the functioning of their mental faculties, so many functions of the guiding awakened heart also occur. The Nirvāṇa Sūtra says:

Though he acts for beings’ benefit
In the garb of Indra or Brahmā,
The world cannot realize this.
And the Inconceivable Secrets says:
“The Buddha’s awakened heart is free from ordinary mind’s objects of focus, yet fully knows the analyses and intentions of the ordinary minds of all beings.”

As stated, he gradually leads beings upward from ordinary worldly talk, annihilation, and permanence, finally drawing them onto the Buddhist path and establishing them in knowledge of every aspect. This is the domain of inconceivable skill in means.

Vajra statement. The claim that only supreme emanations act to guide disciples, while other, inferior ones do not appear, is not exclusively true. Here, everything that can possibly be known—inert matter, non-Buddhists, māras, afflictions, and so forth—does the work of a buddha. The Vimalakīrti Sūtra says:

“Ānanda, there are buddha-fields where the deeds of a buddha are done.” Applying this likewise: light, awakening trees, food, water, pleasure groves, palaces, multistoried buildings, emanations, space, the intervening space, dreams, reflections, moons in water, echoes, illusions, mirages, teaching in letters, never forgetting, enjoyments, the four māras, and the eighty-four thousand gateways of afflictions do the deeds of a buddha.[^N-C-083]

notes.problem: The opening citation leaves the operative item unspecified; the next line says to apply the construction to a list.
notes.treatment: Keep the abbreviated opening as supplied and retain every listed instrument.
notes.uncertainty: The complete quotation may identify an initial item absent here.
notes.review_action: Check the quotation boundary and its first omitted or abbreviated instrument.

english: And the Teaching of the Transformations of the Bodhisattvas’ Sphere of Skillful Means says:[^N-C-084]

notes.problem: The title reads འཁྲུལ་པ delusion where a transformation/display title is likely.
notes.treatment: Use Transformations provisionally in the title without changing the Tibetan.
notes.uncertainty: The source title has not been authenticated.
notes.review_action: Identify the sūtra and check the title spelling.

english: “Mañjuśrī, the other non-Buddhist wanderers who appear in this buddha-field should also be understood as the Tathāgata’s inconceivable blessing and skill in means. Why? They all abide at the gateway of inconceivable liberation and, through skill in means, lovingly lead [beings] onward to definite emergence in the perfections. Without abandoning attention to the Three Jewels, they have all reached the supreme culmination of thoroughly maturing beings.”[^N-C-085]

notes.problem: The guiding/loving phrase is irregular; ཀུན་ཏུ་དཔྱོད་པ་བ may be a defective form of the wanderer designation. Attention is a whole-construction use of ཡིད་ལ་བྱ.
notes.treatment: Translate wanderers and lovingly lead provisionally; bracket [beings] as the implicit beneficiary. Use attention for the whole construction rather than mechanically treating ཡིད as an independent entity.
notes.uncertainty: Exact source forms and compound interpretation need review.
notes.review_action: Collate the passage and review the scoped attention construction.

english: Likewise, this is taught at limitless length in the Questions of Sāgaramati, the Pervasion of All Phenomena, and many other sūtras. Doing the work through desire, hatred, and bewilderment is illustrated respectively by the monk Tenpé Lodrö; Aṅgulimāla and the Blessed Buddha Delightful to Behold; and Pūraṇa Kāśyapa.[^N-C-086]

notes.problem: The narrative names are compressed, especially Aṅgulimāla and Delightful to Behold; the reference treats the latter as an ordinary description.
notes.treatment: Retain the threefold respectively relation and provisionally group the names as written.
notes.uncertainty: Whether Delightful to Behold is a separate Buddha name or qualifies another figure is unresolved.
notes.review_action: Identify the three narratives and verify all agents.

english: Accordingly, the Tantra of Authentic Union says, “Dust, darkness, and strength of heart also act for beings’ benefit.”[^N-C-087]

notes.problem: The three may be guṇa terminology (rajas, tamas, sattva), but the source supplies Tibetan labels and no explanation.
notes.treatment: Retain literal dust, darkness, and strength of heart provisionally rather than silently asserting the Sanskrit identification.
notes.uncertainty: The technical identification remains open.
notes.review_action: Check the tantra quotation and decide whole-expression terminology.

english: Although all these do the work, it does not happen before the time is ripe. The Pervasion of All Phenomena says, “For example, fire abides in every kind of wood, yet unless conditions and exertion are complete, it does not blaze or do what is needed. Likewise, buddhas abide in all knowables, yet unless conditions such as faith are complete, they do not appear or do their work.” So it is said.

Vajra statement. Some say that buddhas awaken in different fields, pure and impure and varied in shape. Here, it is held that awakening must occur throughout the basic space of phenomena without exception, because the Sugata is fully and completely awakened to all phenomena. Thus the Extensive Play says:
“Brahmā, I have not awakened in a delimited aspect, within a measure. Brahmā, in an immeasurable and undelimited aspect, I shall fully accomplish the evenness of all phenomena.”[^N-C-088]

notes.problem: The line has shall fully accomplish, without an explicit awakening verb; the reference supplies awakening.
notes.treatment: Retain the future accomplishment wording rather than silently replacing it with a standard sūtra formula.
notes.uncertainty: A missing syllable or shortened formula is possible.
notes.review_action: Compare the cited Extensive Play passage.

english: And the Mother says, “Fully and completely awakened to all phenomena.” It also says, “Those who wish to awaken fully and completely to all phenomena should train in the perfection of discerning knowing.”

The Avataṃsaka teaches awakening in one hundred koṭis of four-continent [world systems] within this very three-thousandfold world system. It is also taught at limitless length in the Heroic Progress, the Source of Jewels, the Benefit to Aṅgulimāla, and so forth.[^N-C-089]

notes.problem: The reference is blank at U04285; the titles are abbreviated and unverified. The quantity modifies four-continent systems, not individual continents or buddhas.
notes.treatment: Retain one hundred koṭis and supply [world systems]; translate the title list provisionally.
notes.uncertainty: Exact titles and the referent of Benefit to Aṅgulimāla remain open.
notes.review_action: Identify the cited works and check the numerical unit.

english: If this were not established, the result of limitless accumulations would be less than a universal monarch, for the Avataṃsaka speaks of a universal monarch ruling [world systems] as numerous as the particles in ten oceans of world systems. Therefore the essential point of generating the ordinary mind [of awakening] is later awakening everywhere.[^N-C-090]

notes.problem: The object ruled and awakening qualifier of ordinary mind are abbreviated.
notes.treatment: Supply [world systems] for the particle comparison and [of awakening] for the established local compound.
notes.uncertainty: The count’s precise nesting should be checked.
notes.review_action: Verify the cosmological comparison and compound scope.

english: Vajra statement. Emanation embodiments arising through the power of birth are supreme—
Source annotation: the twelve deeds.

—or inferior: hearers and solitary victors, artisans, and birth [emanations] such as rabbits, making four. Those arising through cultivation, such as the prostitute who subdued Tenpé Lodrö, are said to have no cause, to arise as mere transformations, and to require no results of virtue or nonvirtue. Taking those who say this as the subject:[^N-C-091]

notes.problem: སྒྱེ་བ reads sack rather than the likely birth; the fourfold enumeration and the separate cultivated emanation are compressed. The prostitute is the subduer, not someone subdued by Tenpé Lodrö.
notes.treatment: Use birth [emanations] as an explicitly provisional contextual reading, keep four, and preserve the agent relationship. U04293 remains a separate source annotation.
notes.uncertainty: The exact fourfold taxonomy and source spelling remain unresolved.
notes.review_action: Check the classification and narrative; do not flatten the source annotation into main prose.

english: A causeless emanation would be impossible, because no phenomenon independent of everything is established. It is “the intrinsic nature of a rabbit.” If this is not established, accept the position of the followers of Bṛhaspati! Accordingly:[^N-C-092]

notes.problem: The example says intrinsic nature of a rabbit; the intended impossibility may require a missing horn, but that word is absent.
notes.treatment: Retain the exact rabbit assertion in quotation marks and do not insert horns.
notes.uncertainty: The logical example is unresolved.
notes.review_action: Collate U04300 and preserve any correction as a separate editorial decision.

english:
Blessed One, skilled in dependence on causes,
Never possessing views of the two extremes,
You teach those ripened results of karma.[^N-C-093]

notes.problem: The source has མཇའ where the repeated quotation elsewhere reads མཐའ.
notes.treatment: Translate extremes provisionally using the exact internal parallel at U04190, without source modification.
notes.uncertainty: A transcript error is likely but not authenticated to a witness.
notes.review_action: Check the unusual spelling in a physical or independent source.

english: The Dispelling of Ajātaśatru’s Regret says, “All phenomena follow their causes.” And the statement, “When the time for guiding arrives, he enters the deep absorption called such-and-such,” refers to accomplishing a cause. In general, all phenomena are emanations. The Mother says:
“Subhūti, some are emanations of afflictions.” Likewise, there are emanations of karma, hearers, solitary victors, and buddhas.
As this says, according to your position it would follow that everything is causeless. Therefore [emanations] have causes deriving from the Buddha himself.[^N-C-094]

notes.problem: The subject of having causes is not repeated; རྒྱུད་པ functions verbally as deriving/transmitting here, not as the technical noun continuum.
notes.treatment: Supply [emanations] and render deriving locally.
notes.uncertainty: The grammatical relation is supported by the preceding argument; terminology use remains scoped.
notes.review_action: Review the supplied subject and verbal use.

english: Vajra statement. Some say that although the two form embodiments and primordial knowing are absent from the Buddha’s Dharma embodiment, they are appearances to others—the disciples. Here, a buddha is seen when three things come together: attainment of the completely pure Dharma embodiment; the commitment to establish beings at buddhahood; and disciples’ appearance of faith, through having accumulated the karma to meet a buddha. The Supreme Continuum says:

Just as the reflection of the lord of gods’ body
Appears on a pure ground of lapis lazuli,
So, on the pure ground of beings’ ordinary minds,
The reflection of the Lord of Sages’ embodiment arises.
The Eight Thousand teaches this through the example of a vīṇā. And the Foundation of Schism says:[^N-C-095]

notes.problem: The reference is blank at U04333; this is a textual title containing གཞི rather than an occurrence of the ontological Ground.
notes.treatment: Translate Foundation of Schism provisionally as a whole title.
notes.uncertainty: The exact title identification is not independently checked.
notes.review_action: Verify the Vinaya textual source and approve the title.

english: “The buddhas, the blessed ones, are not through a single embodiment, not through a single condition, not through a single root of virtue.”

Thus primordial knowing, qualities, and enlightened activity arise when causes and conditions gather. The inconceivable embodiments and primordial knowing, and their deeds, are the sphere of buddhas alone; hence they are not solely appearances to others. What is called a buddha is the embodiment of dependent arising and so forth.

Vajra statement. Some say it is certain that emanation embodiments arise only from aspiration, the conventional ordinary mind of awakening. It is not restricted to that alone: complete enjoyment embodiment and emanation embodiment may also arise respectively from aspiration and engagement.

The result of this aspiration, which includes within conceptual mind all beings equal to the limits of space, is immeasurable. Because desire and aspiration are generated toward the buddhas of the limitless ten directions, complete enjoyment embodiment arises from aspiration. Depending on that generation of ordinary mind [of awakening], each distinct root of virtue gives rise to an individual emanation embodiment. Awakening throughout the basic space of phenomena and holding embodiments to be dependent arising rest on the essential point that emanations have causes.[^N-C-096]

notes.problem: The awakening qualifier is implicit in the short compound.
notes.treatment: Supply [of awakening], following the explicit compound at U04343 and the prior terminology record N-C-079.
notes.uncertainty: The supply is contextually strong.
notes.review_action: Review the whole-expression terminology once for this section.

english: The former case is like the potter Yangpé Ö, who generated desire and aspiration toward a single buddha.[^N-C-097]

notes.problem: The potter’s name is irregular and not identifiable with confidence; the reference turns it into ordinary light.
notes.treatment: Retain Yangpé Ö provisionally as a name rather than replace it with a conjectured known figure.
notes.uncertainty: The antecedent of former case and the name remain open.
notes.review_action: Identify the potter narrative and check the source spelling.

english: Vajra statement. Some say the three embodiments teach separately, respectively: in the palace of the basic space of phenomena, in Akaniṣṭha, and at Vulture Peak and so forth; to retinues of buddhas, tenth-ground bodhisattvas, and those of the three vehicle lineages; the profound Dharma of the unborn, the Great Vehicle, and various vehicles; at the three times of timelessness beyond the three times, perpetual uninterrupted duration, and the occasion for guiding.[^N-C-098]

notes.problem: The three temporal categories are compressed and contain repeated དུས; རྒྱུན་འཁོར is unusual.
notes.treatment: Keep the threefold respectively structure across place, retinue, teaching, and time; render the temporal categories provisionally.
notes.uncertainty: The first and second temporal expressions require verification.
notes.review_action: Review the four parallel triples and exact temporal readings.

english: Here, the three embodiments abide without difference. The Supreme Continuum says:

It is pure because intrinsic nature is pure
And habitual tendencies have been abandoned.
The complete pacification of elaborations
Of self and selflessness is the supreme self.
It is bliss because the aggregates of the mental faculty’s intrinsic nature
And their causes have been reversed.[^N-C-099]

notes.problem: The relation between mental faculty, intrinsic nature, and aggregates is compressed and potentially defective.
notes.treatment: Retain all three components in their apparent modifier chain; do not silently substitute a familiar version.
notes.uncertainty: Whether the mental-faculty phrase qualifies aggregates is unresolved.
notes.review_action: Collate the quoted Supreme Continuum verse.

english: Thus that very Dharma embodiment, endowed with the four characteristics, is the complete enjoyment embodiment adorned with major and minor marks. The inseparable functioning of those two for beings’ benefit is the emanation embodiment. Accordingly, the Moon Lamp says:[^N-C-100]

notes.problem: The prose states four characteristics, while the preceding excerpt visibly discusses purity, self, and bliss only.
notes.treatment: Retain four and do not manufacture an omitted fourth verse.
notes.uncertainty: The quotation may be deliberately abbreviated.
notes.review_action: Check the quotation’s extent and the intended four-characteristic set.

english:
The embodiment has the characteristic of space;
The buddha-field is likewise.
Powers, liberations, and meditative stabilities—
All have one characteristic.
So it is said. Therefore they differ only by conceptual distinction.[^N-C-101]

notes.problem: ལྡོག་པ is a scholastic distinction term here, not simple reversal.
notes.treatment: Use conceptual distinction provisionally.
notes.uncertainty: Its precise technical account is not supplied.
notes.review_action: Review the term in relation to the embodiment argument.

english: Vajra statement. Some say that the buddhas of the three times, after performing their deeds, pass into nirvāṇa like a fire whose fuel is exhausted and abide in the Akaniṣṭha palace of the basic space of phenomena.

Here, all buddhas of the three times abide in the elemental continua of beings. From the first generation of the resolve for awakening until the holy Dharma abides, they have accomplished the benefit of limitless beings; it is impossible for them now to abide with little concern. This is also established [elsewhere]. The Moon Lamp says:[^N-C-102]

notes.problem: The ཐུགས་ལས idiom may concern little concern or little activity, not a small mind. གཏན་ལ་ཕབ་པ may be a source title rather than a statement.
notes.treatment: Use little concern provisionally and bracket [elsewhere] for the unresolved citation transition; use elemental continua for ཁམས་རྒྱུད.
notes.uncertainty: Both the idiom and possible source title remain open.
notes.review_action: Review the idiom and identify whether གཏན་ལ་ཕབ་པ is a cited work.

english: “Not abiding in nirvāṇa, abiding in authentic evenness, abiding on the ground of seeing all beings.”
Accordingly, all tathāgatas of the three times, with none missing, abide in the elemental continuum of each being, because they have no deeds other than beings’ benefit. How do they abide?

Because the perfect buddha embodiment proliferates,
Because suchness is indivisible,
And because the lineage is present,
All embodied beings always possess the buddha heart.

Because buddha primordial knowing enters the multitude of beings,
Because its stainless intrinsic nature is nondual,
And because the result is imputed to the buddha lineage,
All wandering beings are said to possess the buddha heart.[^N-C-103]

notes.problem: Buddha-heart and lineage/element terminology lacks whole-expression entries; using essence for སྙིང་པོ would overlap the active ངོ་བོ entry.
notes.treatment: Use buddha heart provisionally for སངས་རྒྱས་སྙིང་པོ and lineage for རིགས; retain the source’s result-imputation relation.
notes.uncertainty: A final tathāgatagarbha/gotra terminology decision remains open.
notes.review_action: Review these compounds together with buddha element and elemental continuum usages.

english: The Dharma Lord takes these words to mean that all buddhas abide in beings’ continua, differing from the dialecticians. Therefore one should abandon bad activity of the three gates. If one does not, their awakened hearts are displeased; if one does, they are pleased, and there is an opening for enlightened activity to engage.[^N-C-104]

notes.problem: The subject of displeasure/pleasure is unstated; the reference assigns it to oneself, which conflicts with the honorific and the preceding buddhas.
notes.treatment: Read the buddhas as the implicit experiencers, preserving awakened heart in the first clause.
notes.uncertainty: The implicit subject is contextually strong but requires confirmation.
notes.review_action: Review the referent and causal relation to enlightened activity.

english: This is the section of sixteen vajra statements together with one supplementary statement, summarizing the essential meanings of resultant buddhahood. Thus the explanation of all seven sections is fully completed.
